- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then gradually decline — suggesting a lag in recognizing sustained upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, forecasts often overcorrect downward, failing to capture the lingering upward trend.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model underestimates sustained upward trends, especially when recent history shows strong momentum.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days are often too low, indicating a failure to account for recent upward momentum or policy-driven volatility.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher prices in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 15–25), possibly due to overfitting to recent high values.
- When true prices rise sharply, forecasts lag behind by 1–3 days, suggesting a delay in adjusting to new market conditions.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt volatility or sudden policy shifts, leading to underestimation of price spikes.
